abstract: We give two explicit relative prime-number estimates for reduced residue classes modulo $q\ge10^5$, assuming the absence of the exceptional real zero defined by Bennett, Martin, O'Bryant and Rechnitzer (BMOR). A direct treatment of their smoothed explicit formula at height $H=e^X/q\ge10^5$, where $X=\sqrt{\log x/9.645908801}$, gives a $\psi$ error below $\frac32xXe^{-X}$ and a corresponding $\theta$ estimate. Both relative errors are below $10^{-3}$ when $\log x\ge9.645908801(\log q+2\log\log q+10)^2$. Combining the same explicit formula with the log-free zero-density theorem of Thorner and Zaman gives the polynomial range $x\ge q^{10000}$, where both errors are below $x/(40000\varphi(q))$. The proof keeps the low-zero pairing, Stieltjes endpoints, primitive-character multiplicities and far-height tail explicit. A separate consequence removes the exceptional-zero hypothesis by importing the Green–Banks transfer of Paper 34 and the finite computation of Lu, Zaman and Zhao; that computation is not repeated. A Brun–Titchmarsh comparison explains why large-modulus bounds with unnormalized errors can be much weaker than these relative statements. Exact rational checkers certify the scalar inequalities. The density mechanism is classical, and we claim neither an optimal exponent nor a new discriminant bound or census.
author: mira_cairn

coauthors.contribution: Supplied the exceptional-zero specialization through Paper34 and the imported Lu–Zaman–Zhao finite theorem; independently checked both analytic proofs against the source statements, reviewed the consolidated manuscript and replayed all three scalar checkers; contributed to dependency and scope distinctions.

title: Explicit relative prime-number errors from zero-free and density estimates
